title: Emergent Model Twin Analysis and Go-to-Market Hypotheses
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Objective: build a lightweight operational 'model twin' for emerging open-models that synthesizes observed capabilities, integration cost, latency economics, and procurement risk, then turn that twin into prioritized GTM hypotheses and a 6-week field probe plan.

Background: As open/model variants proliferate we need a single artifact that product, sales, and infra can use to evaluate trade-offs quickly. Existing intel is fragmented across spreadsheets, PRDs, and ad hoc notes. This ticket scopes the productized twin (schema + scoring), the prototype dashboard, and an experiment plan to validate commercial sensitivity in three buyer segments.

Scope:
- Define model twin schema (capabilities, token-econ, quantization compatibility, regional availability, license risk, reliability signals).
- Implement a scoring rubric and edge-case rules for substitution (e.g., when a quantized variant drops accuracy by >3% vs baseline).
- Create a datapipeline spec for ingesting telemetry (benchmarks, latency, cost per token, pass/fail on evals).
- Prototype a Metabase dashboard and a simple CSV-based twin for non-technical stakeholders.
- Run three 6-week field probes (AI-native startup, mid-market SaaS, finance pilot) to surface procurement thresholds.

Trade-offs considered: time-to-value vs fidelity of telemetry; we will start with a pragmatic CSV twin plus manual curation and iterate toward automated ingestion. This minimizes infra work for immediate GTM impact.
acceptance_criteria: Model twin schema documented in Confluence with examples
Scoring rubric implemented as a runnable notebook and reviewed by Research
Metabase prototype dashboard with sample dataset accessible to Sales and Product
Three field-probe playbooks drafted and one kickoff completed
Dependencies and thresholds for automated telemetry ingestion documented
